GIS Lectures 3–4 · Narrated animation

Linear Referencing

How road agencies say where things are: by route and milepoint instead of latitude and longitude. Follows one real crash on SR 154 in Fulton County from its route ID to a straight-line diagram, the curve-crash comparison with the 150 ft buffer, and dynamic segmentation.

0:00 / 0:00

Transcript

Click a sentence to jump there. Keyboard: space plays and pauses, the arrow keys move one sentence, F toggles full screen.

    Voice: Microsoft Andrew (neural text-to-speech). Road segments: GDOT state-route segments (GeorgiaRoadSegments_SR), simplified to 15 ft, with milepoints at each vertex interpolated between the segment ends; curves: synthetic, detected from the bends in those centerlines and located on the route by projecting their end vertices; crashes: a synthetic table of 480 invented crashes; county outlines: U.S. Census Bureau via us-atlas. The curves and crashes are synthetic and only illustrate the method. Companion lab: the Linear Referencing Lab.
